reservation-flow.title: Reservation Flow Redesign
reservation-flow.shortDesc: +20% reserve completion rate and cut booking time from 7 minutes to 3 minutes
reservation-flow.description: Redesigned the reservation flow for IranHotelOnline, a high-traffic booking platform with 500K+ MAU, to reduce friction and improve conversion rates.
reservation-flow.context: IranHotelOnline is a high-traffic hotel booking platform serving over 500,000+ monthly active users. The reservation flow is the primary revenue-driving funnel, making its performance critical to business growth.

problem.description: Despite strong traffic, the booking funnel showed clear performance issues:
issues: Long average booking completion time (around 7–8 minutes)
Frequent rage clicks and hesitation signals
goals: Improve clarity and user confidence throughout the flow

research.description: This project was conducted as a cross-functional effort, with close collaboration between Design, Product, and Engineering.
methods: Reviewed Google Analytics data together with the PM to identify drop-off points and bottlenecks
Analyzed Microsoft Clarity session recordings and heatmaps to observe real user behavior
Evaluated feature ideas with the PM based on data-driven hypotheses
Validated technical feasibility of design changes with the PO and front-end developers
Identified key friction points through behavioral patterns rather than assumptions
insights: Form-heavy steps caused hesitation and abandonment
Some steps did not align with users' mental models of a "standard booking flow"
Redundant inputs increased cognitive load and slowed decision-making

processLeadership.description: Beyond execution, I defined and led the entire design process—from stakeholder alignment to post-launch monitoring. This involved navigating technical constraints, managing cross-functional friction, and establishing quality standards that balanced speed with excellence.

framework.title: 7-Step Design Process Framework
steps: Guerrilla User Testing (pre-design) - Conducted in-person usability tests with non-technical users using think-aloud protocol to identify core friction points
Data Analysis (Microsoft Clarity) - Analyzed session recordings, heatmaps, and rage click patterns to validate assumptions with behavioral data
PM Alignment Meeting - Presented research findings and negotiated scope (e.g., debated removing low-value checkboxes vs. stakeholder requests)
PO/Dev Constraint Mapping - Discussed technical limitations upfront to avoid designing features requiring unavailable backend logic
Design Execution - Created high-fidelity prototypes based on validated insights and technical feasibility
Second-Round User Testing (staging) - Tested live implementation on staging environment to catch mobile-specific issues (e.g., keyboard + bottom sheet overlap)
Rigorous QA & Launch - Enforced strict design quality standards (2px max tolerance) and collaborated with developers through documented feedback

challenges.title: Stakeholder Negotiation
challenges.issue: PM wanted to keep low-value service checkboxes for certain stakeholders, but data showed they confused users and added no conversion value.
challenges.solution: Presented Clarity heatmap data showing 73% of users ignored these checkboxes. PM agreed to deprioritize them in v1 and validate with data later.

challenges.title: Technical Constraints
challenges.issue: PO + developers flagged that some features (like real-time logic for dynamic fields) required unavailable backend work outside the current sprint capacity.
challenges.solution: Adjusted designs to align with current backend capabilities. Prioritized UI improvements requiring only front-end changes and deferred heavy features post-launch.

challenges.title: Critical Mobile Bug Discovery
challenges.issue: During second-round testing on staging, discovered that when mobile keyboard opened, bottom sheet input fields became inaccessible—users literally couldn't submit the form.
challenges.solution: Immediately notified dev team. Redesigned bottom sheet positioning with safe padding and tested 3 different layouts to ensure keyboard + sheet coexisted comfortably.

challenges.title: Developer Friction Over Strict Standards
challenges.issue: When I enforced rigorous QA (flagging even 2px errors), developers felt I was being overly critical. After fixes, new issues appeared, leading to rework fatigue.
challenges.solution: Held alignment session with PO, PM, and Dev. Established '2-strike rule': designs rejected more than twice for quality issues required root cause analysis. Devs improved attention to detail, and rework dropped 60%.

challenges.title: Time Investment for Post-Launch Monitoring
challenges.issue: I monitored Microsoft Clarity and Google Analytics for 5 consecutive days after launch—very time-consuming, and it wasn't clear if it was worthwhile.
challenges.solution: Monitoring caught a minor issue (mobile toggle sizes were too small). Realized careful post-launch observation can catch things standard data analysis misses. Now this is standard practice for high-risk launches.

impact: Defined a 7-step process framework now used by the design team for high-risk projects
Two-round user testing (pre-design + staging) caught a critical mobile bug that would have reduced mobile conversion by 15-20%
Strict quality standards led to more consistent design across the platform (QA rejection rate dropped 60% after '2-strike rule')
Stakeholder alignment sessions reduced post-launch change requests by 80% (expectations were clearer upfront)
Process documentation helped a junior designer successfully adopt this framework for payment flow redesign (launched with 92% quality score)

solution.description: The final solution was a streamlined reservation flow featuring:
features: Clear progress indicators and user feedback
solution.implementation: Delivered designs with full specifications and worked closely with QA to ensure precise implementation. I personally QA-checked the implementation end-to-end.

learnings: When we removed the 'Passenger Details' step and merged it with 'Review,' the #1 drop-off point disappeared—sometimes the best design decision is deletion, not addition
When we showed price in real-time within the form, user trust increased by 28% (measured via exit survey)—transparency matters
Engineers flagged a backend constraint on autofill logic that could have delayed launch by 2 weeks—our early collaboration saved us from redesigning
Iranian users expect different payment flows than international users—localization isn't just translation, it's adapting behavior

design-system.title: Design System Creation
design-system.shortDesc: Cut feature design time from 5 days to 3 days with a unified component library
design-system.description: Built a comprehensive atomic design system for IranHotelOnline to standardize UI components and accelerate the design-to-development workflow.
design-system.context: As the team grew, inconsistent UI patterns emerged across the platform. Designers rebuilt similar components in different ways, and developers implemented the same functionality with different styles. This created maintenance issues and a fragmented user experience.

problem.description: The lack of a unified design language was causing significant inefficiencies:
issues: Designers spent hours recreating common components from scratch
Developers duplicated components with different implementations
Spacing, colors, and typography were inconsistent across pages
Handoff process was slow with constant clarification questions
New team members struggled to learn design patterns
goals: Create a single source of truth for design patterns
Ensure UI consistency across the platform
Reduce onboarding time for new team members
Free up designers to focus on solving problems rather than rebuilding components

research.description: Audited existing patterns and collaborated with stakeholders to understand pain points.
methods: UI inventory across all platform pages
Interviewed designers and developers about their workflow blockers
Analyzed documentation gaps and common questions
Studied best practices from established design systems (Material, Carbon, Atlassian)
Identified most-used components and their variations
insights: Developers wanted clearer specs and reusable code
Designers needed faster access to ready-to-use components

solution.description: Delivered a complete, documented design system featuring:
features: Comprehensive Figma component library with variants and auto-layout
Design tokens covering all visual properties
Usage documentation with examples and best practices
Accessibility guidelines integrated into component specs
solution.implementation: Launched the system incrementally—starting with high-traffic pages to validate adoption, then expanding across the platform.

learnings: Documentation makes the difference between a design system that's used vs. ignored—invest heavily upfront
Start with small, high-impact components rather than trying to build everything at once—adoption matters more than completeness
Hosting regular design system office hours (weekly 30-min sessions) helped address blockers and gather feedback
Aligning component names with dev frameworks (e.g., matching React prop names) removed handoff friction

ihotelhub.title: B2B Platform iHotelHub
ihotelhub.shortDesc: Cut hotel manager task completion time by 45% through dashboard redesign
ihotelhub.description: Redesigned the B2B dashboard for hotel managers to streamline property management, booking oversight, and revenue tracking.
ihotelhub.collaboration: PM, Back-end Developers, Customer Success Team
ihotelhub.context: iHotelHub is a B2B platform used by hotel managers to manage properties, track reservations, and monitor revenue. The legacy interface was cluttered and inefficient, leading to high support tickets and user frustration.

problem.description: Hotel managers faced significant challenges in their workflow:
issues: Critical information was buried in nested menus
No clear visual hierarchy for high-priority tasks
No mobile version (while managers are often on the move)
Difficult system learning curve for new users
goals: Reduce time spent on common tasks

research.description: Conducted extensive research with hotel managers to understand their workflow.
methods: Interviewed 12 hotel managers about their daily tasks and pain points
Shadowed 3 managers throughout their workday to observe real usage patterns
Analyzed support tickets to identify common issues
Reviewed analytics data to see which features were used and where users dropped off
Created user journey maps for key scenarios
insights: 80% of tasks involved checking today's bookings and revenue
Managers needed quick access to guest contact info for urgent issues
Mobile access was critical for managers not at their desks
Data export functionality was heavily used but poorly designed
Visual clutter was overwhelming—managers wanted insights at a glance

solution.description: Delivered a modern, efficient B2B dashboard featuring:
features: Priority-based dashboard showing critical information first
Responsive mobile design that works comfortably on all devices
Simplified navigation with clear information architecture
Advanced search and filtering for bookings and guests
Visual charts for revenue and occupancy insights
Batch operations for managing multiple bookings
solution.implementation: Launched in phases—first the dashboard, then other modules. Provided video tutorials and live training sessions for existing users.

learnings: B2B users prioritize efficiency over beauty—every click matters when you're managing 50+ bookings daily
Mobile-first design isn't just for consumers—hotel managers are constantly on the move
Providing training resources (videos, guides) alongside new features significantly improved adoption
Hoteliers want customizable dashboards—one size doesn't fit all for different property types
